subject: ventures/paid-sick-leave-accrual-calculator
professional: a multi-state payroll / HR compliance specialist who sets up sick-leave accrual policies in payroll systems for small employers. First checks: accrual rate and the employer's permitted caps per state (annual accrual, annual use, balance), size thresholds for paid vs unpaid, front-loading amounts, and whether every state with a statewide law is covered.

evidence.correctness: Ran the engine on 11 cases (node /tmp/claude-0/q92-psl/tool.mjs) and recomputed them in /tmp/claude-0/q92-psl/indep.py from the statutes (cited from knowledge; mgaleg.maryland.gov, law.justia.com and marisstella.app all returned proxy 403, so no statute text was fetched). Right: accrual rates for all 14 states (1/30 most, WA and IL 1/40, NV 0.01923 = 1/52), CA 40 use / 80 balance / 40 front-load (Lab. Code 246 as amended by SB 616), CO 48, NJ 40, NM 64, WA no cap with 40-hour carryover, NV 50-employee threshold, MA 11 / OR 10 / MD 15 paid thresholds, AZ 24 vs 40 at 15, MI 40 vs 72 at 11, NY 40/56 tiers; per-pay-period figures (40 h/week in a 1/30 state = 1.3333 per week, 2.6667 biweekly) all equal. Wrong: Maryland balance cap is 40 in the tool (calc.mjs:28) but Md. Code Lab. & Empl. 3-1305 lets an employer cap the balance at 64 hours and use at 64 hours a year (accrual 40 a year); the tool tells a Maryland employer accrual stops at 40, under-providing up to 24 hours. CA sample 'cost if all used' 1,220.27 per employee / 14,643 for 12 uses the uncapped 55.47 accrued hours, while Lab. Code 246(d) lets the employer limit use to 40 hours a year, so the most that can be used in a year is 880 / 10,560 (39% over); same inconsistency for MN, OR and MD (accrual uncapped whenever a balance cap exists, calc.mjs:78). Front-load alternative uses the large-employer figure for small employers (AZ 10 employees: 40 h = 800 where A.R.S. 23-372 requires 24; MI 8 employees: 72 h = 1,440 where ESTA small-employer amount is 40). Several outputs right, one state's cap wrong and a headline cost overstated, so 2.
evidence.completeness: Every feature the README and page list works end to end in the engine: state picker of 14 states, size-dependent paid/unpaid and use caps, per-pay-period accrual, annual and balance-cap cost, front-load alternative, text summary with sources, print, usage opt-out. No TODOs or stubs. Missing relative to the field (not to the README's own list): CT, RI, VT, ME, AK, NE and DC statewide laws; NY's $1M net-income test is in a note but not an input.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the subject root: 25/25 pass. Seeded 5 mutants with quality_mutate.py: Illinois rate 1/40 -> 1/30 SURVIVED; Maryland balance 40 -> 64 SURVIVED; Washington carryover 40 -> 80 SURVIVED; NY paid threshold 5 -> 6 employees SURVIVED; dropping the 'no balance cap' condition on the accrual cap caught. 4 of 5 survived; IL, CO, NJ, OR, MD, MN and NM values have no test at all, and the test file asserts the author's numbers rather than statute-sourced ones.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (119 lines), index.html (183), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Small pure engine, data-driven state table, strict parsing that rejects rather than clamps, output escaped, no network. Concerns: the cap model conflates use caps and accrual caps (one 'use' field drives both, calc.mjs:75-78), the 'carry' field is read only for 'use40' and otherwise ignored, frontHours Math.max(s.front, 0) is a no-op, front-load is a single number not a size function.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer and no-warranty on page, README and summary; privacy claim backed by page.test.mjs (no fetch/XHR/beacon) and usage events match record() calls. But: README line 3 '14 with statewide paid sick leave laws' reads as the full set while CT, RI, VT, ME, AK, NE and DC also have statewide laws; page header (index.html:62) says 'written from the statutes' while README and calc.mjs:3 say 'from memory WITHOUT network access'; FAQ (index.html:104) says Minnesota's 48 is a use cap, Minn. Stat. 181.9446 caps accrual at 48 a year, not use; the Maryland 40-hour balance cap is stated as law. llms.txt github.io link is rewritten at deploy (source-only, not filed).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a 20-person Maryland shop setting a payroll accrual policy would configure a 40-hour balance cap and be out of compliance; a 12-person California shop reading the headline sees 14,643 a year when the most leave that can be taken is worth 10,560; a 12-person Connecticut employer (covered from 2026-01-01 under Public Act 24-8) cannot pick its state. A multistate employer in the 11 or so correct states gets a fast, right first read.
evidence.domain: Compared with the state statutes (Cal. Lab. Code 246; N.Y. Lab. Law 196-b; RCW 49.46.210; 820 ILCS 192; C.R.S. 8-13.3-403; N.J.S.A. 34:11D-2; M.G.L. c.149 148C; A.R.S. 23-372; ORS 653.606; Md. Lab. & Empl. 3-1304/3-1305; Minn. Stat. 181.9446; MCL 408.964; NMSA 50-17-3; NRS 608.0197). The accrual-rate method and size thresholds match; departures: no distinction between annual accrual cap, annual use cap and balance cap (the three separate employer options most statutes grant), MD caps wrong, size-dependent front-load amounts ignored, MD 12-hour/week coverage floor not modelled, NY income test not modelled, seven statewide jurisdictions absent.

defects.what: Maryland balance cap is 40 hours; Md. Lab. & Empl. 3-1305 lets the employer cap the balance at 64 hours (and use at 64 a year, accrual at 40 a year). The finding tells the employer accrual stops at 40, under-providing up to 24 hours and understating the balance liability (800 vs 1,280 at $20).

'Cost if all used' uses uncapped accrued hours whenever a state has a balance cap (CA, MN, OR, MD), though the statute lets the employer limit use (CA 40 h a year): the CA example headline is 14,643 where the usable maximum is 10,560. The single 'use' field is used as both an accrual cap and a use cap.
Front-load hours ignore employer size: AZ under 15 employees shown 40 h (statute 24), MI 10 or fewer shown 72 h (ESTA small employer 40).

Seven statewide jurisdictions are missing (CT, RI, VT, ME, AK, NE, DC) while the README and VENTURE.yaml describe the 14 as the states 'with statewide paid sick leave laws'; a Connecticut employer with 11+ employees, covered since 2026-01-01, cannot use the tool.
Tests leave 7 of 14 states' values untested; 4 of 5 seeded mutants in the state table and carryover logic survived.
FAQ calls Minnesota's 48 hours a use cap; Minn. Stat. 181.9446 caps annual accrual at 48 (balance 80), not use. The engine's finding text for MN repeats 'use is limited to 48 hours a year'.
Page says rules were 'written from the statutes' while README and calc.mjs say they were written from memory without network access.
New York employers with 4 or fewer employees are always shown as unpaid; 196-b(1)(a) requires paid leave when net income exceeds $1M. Only a note mentions it.
README test command uses a repo-relative glob; the instructions-supported form from the subject root is node --test '*.test.mjs'.

verdict: A small, clean, private calculator whose accrual rates and size thresholds are right for most of its 14 states, but it does not meet the bar. Maryland's balance cap is wrong (40 vs 64 in Lab. & Empl. 3-1305), so a Maryland employer following it would under-provide leave. The California worked example's headline cost overstates what can be used in a year by 39%, because use caps and accrual caps are modelled as one field. Small-employer front-load amounts for AZ and MI are wrong, seven statewide jurisdictions are missing while the README implies the list is complete, and 4 of 5 seeded mutants survived the tests. Correctness 2, claims 2, verification 1.
